It's not in the last few years, but it's something you see talked about again with Titanfall, Battlefront and Rainbow Siege.

A full priced multiplayer only game. And the original risk takers in this were ID Software with Quake 3 Arena. People were very skeptical that a full priced multiplayer only game could sell well. They thought the token effort of a series of bot matches that counted as a single player campaign would just piss people off.

Then a year or so later Unreal Tournament did the same thing, and has had iterations ever since.

But, to Quake and Unreal's credit, these were games that shipped with level editors and mod tools almost out of the box. Quake 3 shipped with 19 deathmatch maps, 6 1v1 maps and 4 CTF maps. Checking wiki's it's looking like Unreal Tournament shipped with even more.

By comparison, Titanfall has 15 maps, Star Wars Battlefront has 12 maps, and Rainbow Six Siege has 11. Near as I'm aware, none of them have a map editor or allow mods.
